newsitem.title: USA: U.S. STOCKS EASE AS INVESTORS TAKE SOME PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. STOCKS EASE AS INVESTORS TAKE SOME PROFITS.

text.p: Wall Street shares backed off opening highs on Thursday, as investors took some profits from recently-strong sectors like technology while watching the bond market ease slightly.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was up eight points to 8267, below its early session gains. The long bond also retreated to trade up only 3/32 at 6.47 percent.
The Nasdaq composite, a source of recent market leadership, paused. It slipped about two points to 1629.

"Even a train has to stop at the station," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp said. "The market has been on an unbelievable run, especially the tech stocks. We are seeing some profit-taking setting in."
Stocks closed at record highs on Wednesday as bond yields declined, pointing to lower long-term rates, and as technology stocks surged.
On Thursday, the bond market focused on a $10 billion Treasury auction of 30-year bonds at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.
